correctness.rationale: The nine-factor list is exhaustive by the fivefold-substitution two-superblock argument. Intransitive subgroup counts are bounded below by the exact 63-block-Parikh census. The published exhaustive classification of the seven transitive degree-seven types, together with actual enumeration of every conjugate of each of the five proper types and parity adjustment for A7/S7, excludes complexity four and supplies the exact attainable spectrum. A standalone checked script derives and asserts all counts; only the group-type classification is imported.

evidence: The source proves that any group with complexity four at selected odd lengths must be transitive; it explicitly poses the remaining issue as an open problem.
At this canonical seven-letter length, all transitive types give counts in {3,5,6,7,8,9}, no 4, by the complete representative-and-conjugate calculation.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: A necessary transitivity condition is not an exclusion of all transitive groups. The new implication is specific: for the ternary Fibonacci image at length seven, both transitive and intransitive possibilities exclude four, and five attainable values above three are witnessed. The source does not assert this finite result.

evidence: The source defines group complexity as orbits of the length-n factor set under coordinate permutations; the equivalent restricted-orbit formulation is used here.
Theorem 7 addresses only nontransitive groups under suitable odd-length conditions.
The finite source factor set consists of one seven-element rotation class and two singleton abelian classes.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The exact equivalence tested is the number of group-orbits on the specified nine-factor set; the zero- and one-based coordinate conventions do not alter orbits. Neither the source criterion nor alternative word wording implies the seven-coordinate full spectrum or rules out transitive value-four witnesses.

originality.rationale: The July 8, 2026 primary paper raises the four-orbit question for ternary minimal complexity and excludes nontransitive witnesses under a necessary condition, but does not compute the special Fibonacci-image spectrum at length seven. Known degree-seven group tables give the group types, not the action on this particular word language. Targeted equivalent and broader-result searches did not identify a prior assertion or implication of the complete spectrum; unindexed parallel computation remains possible.
residual_risks: A complete published classification of degree-seven transitive groups is used rather than reproved.
An unindexed earlier equivalent calculation for this specific finite group-complexity spectrum may exist.
No statement is made beyond length seven or on the general open question.

value.rationale: The source explicitly motivates the missing intermediate group-complexity value four in a ternary Sturmian morphic family. The natural length seven comes from the first nontrivial odd Fibonacci standard factor image psi(01001), not an arbitrary search slice; its full spectrum settles that canonical finite case and shows a genuine transitive obstruction beyond the prior necessary condition. The explicit finite group action certificate is reusable as a benchmark for extensions, though it provides no all-length theorem.
